📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

It has been revealed that united are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot swiftly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a fresh low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”.

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most vital thing for me is the team.

Recent findings suggest that “First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”.

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he mentioned.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”.

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but remarked he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

In a recent development, “It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”.

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:21 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cristiano Ronaldo may have finally departed the international stage, but he still remained a major part of Portugal's story over the past week.

That came after they suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Denmark in the first game since his retirement, their heaviest home loss in competitive history.

In the aftermath of that match, Ronaldo's mother Dolores launched a furious and unprompted attack on the national team, claiming the defeat was just, and added she was happy to see the result.

Despite an emotional and historic tribute to Ronaldo pre-game, Dolores also expressed her unhappiness at what had unfolded, before she claimed the veteran's former international team-mates failed to show him the respect he deserved during his career.

Dolores has not always been an outspoken presence over the years, but has often stepped up to defend her son when she feels necessary.

So, in light of her outburst, Daily Mail Sport has taken a look at other examples of when the mums of footballers have got involved in their careers.

Cristiano Ronaldo's mum became embroiled in her son's row with Portugal's national team after saying she was happy to see them suffer a heavy defeat (Source: Instagram/doloresaveiroofficial).

Veronique Rabiot – Adrien Rabiot.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique has developed a reputation as an uncompromising and fiercely protective negotiator in her role as his agent.

This has seen the French midfielder face several flashpoints in his career, beginning  when Veronique pulled him out of Man City's academy after just six months in 2008 because she felt they were not looking after his interests like they should be.

During his time at PSG, where Rabiot ultimately broke through and spent seven seasons in the first team, Veronique then frequently clashed with the club's hierarchy.

Potential transfers to Roma and Man United during his career have also both collapsed late on, a factor some reports attach to Veronique's role in the deals.

There have been several notable flashpoints on the international stage too, not least when she backed her son's controversial decision to withdraw from France's standby list for the 2018 World Cup.

But that was nothing compared to the aftermath of France's shock exit from Euro 2020 at the last-16 stage.

Veronique made headlines at the time for engaging in a heated confrontation with the parents of Kylian Mbappe and the entourage of Paul Pogba in the stands over on-pitch errors and perceived arrogance during Les Bleus' campaign.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique (centre) has developed a reputation as a formidable force.

As the mother of one of the best footballers on the planet, Fayza Lamari was always likely to be a major powerbroker, and she has played a key role in Kylian Mbappe's career, acting as his chief negotiator and business manager.

This has seen Fayza oversee Mbappe's commercial obligations and image rights, while she played a central role in his dramatic contract extension at PSG in 2022.

She was similarly key when Mbappe joined Real Madrid in 2024. On that occasion, she was credited for helping to secure a huge signing bonus and favourable image rights split for her son.

Fayza hasn't been afraid to publicly stand up for the forward, and she was key in the legal dispute over unpaid salary and bonuses that he felt he was owed by PSG after his exit.

PSG were ultimately ordered to pay Mbappe €60million (£52.5m) by a French court in a major victory for Fayza.

Kylian Mbappe's mum Fayza (also pictured with his brother Ethan) has played a key role in the commercial side of his career.

Sheila Ebana has been a foundational and supportive presence throughout Lamine Yamal's childhood and rise into professional football.

But, alongside regularly attending Yamal's games, Sheila has become a celebrity in her own right after embracing her public profile.

She regularly provides an insight into her life and shares behind the scenes clips with Yamal and his half brother Keyne on social media, racking up 2.8million followers on Instagram and 2.6million on TikTok.

Sheila has also regularly made paid appearances and attended VIP events, including a bizarre Christmas gala dinner that Daily Mail Sport went to in November 2025 where members of the public paid hundreds of pounds for a three-course meal, champagne, entertainment and a meet-and-greet.

To demonstrate how Sheila has embraced her fame, she once responded to online critics by retorting: 'I don't just think I'm famous - I am.'.

Lamine Yamal's mum (pictured below together with his half-brother Keyne) has embraced her celebrity fame.

Denise Bellingham – Jude Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham has often credited his mother Denise for helping to manage his life off the pitch and keep him grounded.

When he moved to Germany to join Borussia Dortmund as a 17-year-old, Denise went with him – before subsequently following the midfielder to Spain after his transfer to Real Madrid – while his father Mark stayed with his brother Jobe.

She is understood to handle his domestic affairs and finances, while Bellingham inadvertently revealed during the 2022 World Cup that she still made his bed.

Denise has generally provided a constant source of advice, logistical support – which has included driving him to training in the past – and organisational help throughout his time in the game.

The England star is clearly appreciative of all she has done, describing her as his 'queen' and 'backbone', and crediting her with helping to keep him level headed throughout the highs and lows of his career.

Jude Bellingham (pictured also with dad Mark and brother Jobe) has described his mum Denise as his 'queen' and 'backbone'.

Marcia Lewis – Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mother Marcia Lewis has played a crucial role in his rise into Arsenal and England's first team.

When Lewis-Skelly entered the Arsenal academy system at the age of eight, Marcia wanted to learn more about football to ensure she could protect and guide her son's progression.

She subsequently qualified as an agent, meaning she now represents Lewis-Skelly, and also enrolled in a Master's degree in Football Business.

Marcia has since taken part in contract negotiations and filtered external pressures away from her son during his development.

She was later inspired to set up the No1Fan.club, a platform that aims to support families who have children in academy football.

The outlet is dedicated to helping navigate various challenges that arise, such as dealing with scouts, agents and the general pressures associated with youth football.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mum Marcia Lewis tried to learn more about the business of football so she would be able to support her son on his journey (Source: Instagram/myleslewisskelly).

Harry Maguire's mother Zoe has taken a more low-profile approach to her son's career than others, yet she has never been afraid to speak out when she feels the need to.

This included back in 2023 when she snapped after years of watching her son face significant abuse, both online and in stadiums.

At the time, Zoe labelled the heat on the defender as 'disgraceful' and 'unacceptable', and said it went 'far beyond' football.

She re-emerged into the public eye three years later when Maguire was snubbed from England's World Cup squad.

After that, she tweeted: 'Absolutely disgusted.'.

In another post addressing Maguire, she added: 'You couldn’t have done anymore. Hold your head high …Disgraceful.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," said local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Los Angeles has become the largest city in the US to ban oil drilling, after years of lawsuits and campaigning by residents who raised the alarm over pollution and potential health risks from nearby wells .

"Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," said local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

The ordinance, approved by the LA City Council on October 28, puts an immediate stop to oil extraction and bans the redrilling or deepening of wells. Existing operations must be phased out within city limits over the next 20 years.

Though LA City is only part of greater Los Angeles, the move affects hundreds of active wells and thousands of inactive ones, many located in working class communities of color.

Industry observers note that "In South LA, working-class families have had corporations drilling across the street from their homes," stated council president Marqueece Harris-Dawson in a statement. "No one should have to live near an oil drilling site.".

Rock Zierman, CEO of the California Independent Petroleum Association (CIPA), told DW, "CIPA believes this ordinance constitutes an unlawful taking of private property.".

LA follows much smaller Culver City, also in California, in moving against urban oil production, and begins the process of ending its long, complex relationship with fossil fuels.

California's oil industry expanded rapidly in the early 20th century, when the state produced roughly a quarter of the world's oil. Lots of that so-called black gold was around LA and as the city grew, homes, schools and businesses were built around existing oil infrastructure.

It has been revealed that today, wells can be found beneath residential areas, close to playgrounds, along the coast and in some of the city's most densely populated and largely working-class neighborhoods. Some have been permanently sealed or plugged for decades, while others remain active or are idle.

According to recent reports, under California law, an idle well is one that has not produced oil for two years. Unlike plugged wells, they can potentially return to production.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Residents living near the active and inactive wells report strong odors, headaches, nausea and breathing difficulties. Another concern is air quality. Oil wells can release toxic pollutants, including benzene and hydrogen sulfide, and research has linked proximity to oil extraction with higher rates of respiratory illness and reduced lung function.

But both active and idle wells can also leak methane — a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change — while residents say occasional accidents or breakages send oil flowing down city streets.

"Frontline communities have been experiencing or have experienced for decades living near these toxic sites and having to pay for that with their health," mentioned Miranda, a policy director with Esperanza Community Housing, a nonprofit providing affordable housing services.

Sources indicate that miranda told DW she and her mother both have asthma. The council vote "definitely represents hope," she added.

LA City Council initially approved an ordinance to phase out oil extraction back in 2022 after successful lobbying by residents like Wendy Miranda. But oil companies challenged the measure in court, with industry groups successfully arguing that the city lacked the legal authority to impose the ban.

California subsequently passed legislation giving local governments greater power to regulate and restrict oil and gas operations, putting the possibility of a phaseout back on the table.

In an emailed statement to DW, CIPA CEO Rock Zierman said energy companies were prepared to challenge the new ordinance.

Zierman added that it would make city residents more dependent on foreign oil from countries with lower environmental standards when they are "already struggling" with high gas prices.

"It sends the jobs, investment and revenue elsewhere while leaving Californians to pay the bill," stated Zierman.

Sources indicate that the relationship between local oil production and prices at the pump is not straightforward and is influenced by a number of factors, according to the California Energy Commission, the state's main energy policy agency. Those include the cost of crude oil, refining, transportation, distribution and local taxes.

Sources indicate that even though the US is the world's largest oil producer, it exports and imports crude oil, as well as refined petroleum products. Because oil is traded globally, US residents are exposed to the same price fluctuations as people elsewhere, no matter how much of the fossil fuel is produced domestically.

Industry observers note that california's oil industry and the amount of oil it produces have been steadily declining since the 1980s. In the coastal lowlands known as the LA Basin, output is 43% lower than eight years ago, with the amount of oil extracted falling more rapidly than the number of open wells.

According to recent reports, when wells stop producing, it is up to the oil operators to remove equipment and plug them. The state agency that regulates oil and gas, CalGEM, and the LA fire department oversee plugging operations, and also seal wells for which no-one takes responsibility.

But many have not yet been plugged — some 80% of idle wells in LA have been inactive for more than eight years, and about a third for over a century.

The cost of plugging a well also varies widely, with estimates ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars. California law requires operators to submit plugging plans or face annual fines that increase with the amount of time the well has been idle.

According to recent reports, but those fines aren't always paid. According to CalGEM's own data, the agency collected just $1 million out of $36 million (€32 million) in fines in 2025.

It has been revealed that A report by Carbon Tracker also found that if all future profits from oil companies operating in California went to decommissioning wells, the state would still face a shortfall of $7 billion. The cost would by default fall to taxpayers, according to Carbon Tracker.

Miranda told DW that the next step for community activists is to reduce the 20-year timeline and have the oil sector "pay for this cleanup."  For now, she is states both she and her mother are hopeful that future generations "can have better health and breathe cleaner air.".

Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, announced shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.
  • The Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again.
  • "Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," remarked Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, announced shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.

The Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again. They had been barred from doing so since shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

"Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," remarked Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.

In a recent development, "Several championships are only weeks away, and changes to participation affect many people; players, teams, organizing committees and host cities," he said. "We will work closely with all of them to find practical solutions.".

The first tournament the CAS decision applies to is the World Juniors, to be held beginning on December 26 in Canada. Just how it will affect the tournament is not clear. Hockey Canada mentioned it was in contact with the IIHF and had briefed Prime Minister Mark Carney's government on the decision.

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand told public broadcaster CBC that she is "not comfortable" with allowing a Russian team to take part in the tournament in Alberta.

"This is a very unwelcome decision given the geopolitical situation, given the actions of Russia," she noted. "All options are on the table, and I will say, again, I greet this decision with great disappointment.".

Canada's secretary of state for sport, Adam van Koeverden, appeared to rule out Russian athletes being granted visas for the tournament.

"Canada will maintain restrictions on the participation of Russian athletes at events hosted in Canada that receive funding from the Government of Canada and explore further options to ensure that the Russian government is held accountable," he noted in a statement.

Germany is also considering its options as it prepares to host the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Düsseldorf and Mannheim in May.

"The German government takes a very critical view of the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, a government spokesman remarked on Sunday, according to the DPA news agency.

"The German government will discuss possible consequences of the ruling, including for the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany, with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) promptly.".

Sources indicate that the DEB's chief executive, Frank Lutz, is to travel to Berlin to discuss the matter with government officials this week. Speaking on broadcaster MagentaSport on the weekend, he conceded that surrendering Germany's hosting rights for the lucrative tournament was a possibility.

According to recent reports, "I do not want to paint a black picture. I do not want to call the World Championship into question either. But of course, we at the DEB also have to consider the option of handing back this championship," he said.

Several other national ice hockey federations have expressed disappointment at the CAS decision, including those of Ukraine, Sweden, Finland, and Czechia.

The International Olympic Committee opened the door for Russian athletes to return to international competition when it lifted its ban of the Russian Olympic Committee in July. However, the IIHF had already decided to continue to exclude Russian teams for the 2026-27 season – over security concerns. The CAS decision – handed down after an appeal by Russia – found this reasoning was insufficiently proven.

The Kremlin's reaction to the ruling was, unsurprisingly, positive.

"Russia is returning to world hockey. This place rightfully belongs to us, and discrimination in hockey has been brought to an end," Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev told state television channel Vesti.

A boycott of the World Juniors, Men's World Championships or other tournaments by individual nations is now emerging as a real possibility.

"We are at the moment working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen mentioned in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday evening.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

By Tuesday afternoon, the Finland-led effort was gaining steam, with Sweden, Norway and Denmark making similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson stated in a statement.

This came shortly after Norway said it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

According to recent reports, "Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors tournament.

There has been the suggestion, that having won this victory at the CAS, Russia's next focus could be on football, where its national and club teams remain excluded from international competitions.

Russian FA general secretary Maxim Mitrofanov told state news agency Tass that there "should be one rule for all.".

World football's governing body FIFA allowed a Russia boys' team to play under its national flag in the inaugural Under-15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan, which kicked off last week and ends on Saturday.

It has been revealed that this article was originally published on November 2, 2026. It was updated on November 3 with the statement from the Finnish Ice Hockey Association. It was later updated with the statements from the Swedish, Norwegian and Danish federations.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone.
  • Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, presently above Juventus and Napoli in the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By FABRIZIO FERRARI FOR DAILY MAIL SPORT.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.

Not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone. It is a town of 42,000 best known for many years as the birthplace of 20th-century screen icon Marcello Mastroianni and global hotelier Carmine Forte, but now the talk of Italian football.

Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, presently above Juventus and Napoli in the table.

Armed with the second-lowest budget in the league, they have regularly started with seven Italian players – the most in the league – including Antonio Raimondo, a 22-year-old striker on loan from Bologna, who scored nine goals in 10 appearances before being halted by injury at the start of this month.

The majority owner is Newly introduced York investment fund Clara Vista, who are part of the consortium behind Ipswich Town, and the head coach is Massimiliano Alvini, who has drawn comparisons to Roberto De Zerbi for both the high-intensity elements of his style and his rise from the humble depths of Italian football.

Only 18 months ago, in May 2025, they looked set to slide into the third tier, bound for a relegation play-off until Brescia were deducted points to hand Frosinone an unlikely stay of execution.

According to recent reports, A month later a newly introduced sporting director, Renzo Castagnini, arrived and installed Alvini, who kept faith in most of the squad that had survived only by the skin of its teeth. Survival was again the sole aim. Yet from the very first Coppa Italia fixture Frosinone began to turn heads, beating Monza, a team widely tipped for promotion.

By the end of the season, they had finished as runners-up behind Venezia and above Monza who were promoted via the play-offs. It was Frosinone’s fourth promotion to Serie A and by far the most beautiful because nobody saw it coming.

Massimiliano Alvini was recognised as the best coach of Serie B at the 35th edition of the FIGC Panchina D'Oro Awards on Monday.

Frosinone Calcio players celebrated their victory against Lecce in October.

Much of the credit belongs to Alvini, who was named by his fellow managers on Monday as Serie B’s best coach for 2025-26. The 56-year-old Tuscan played at an amateur level until a serious injury forced him to quit at 30. His coaching career began in the same lowly ranks for Italian football.

It has been revealed that he and his brother Walter sold shoe soles for a living. Increasingly, Walter would be asked to cover at work as his brother followed his newly introduced passion, travelling to study the training sessions of established coaches, including Luciano Spalletti at Roma and Maurizio Sarri at Empoli.

Alvini remains grounded and stubbornly modest despite eight promotions and the sudden spotlight.

If the season ended today, Frosinone would qualify for Europe but perhaps the most incredible part of the story was improvements made last season by individual players who had barely registered in the previous season.

Sources indicate that notably Fares Ghedjemis, who went from scoring two goals to 15. Also Castagnini signings such as Giacomo Calo and others including Giorgi Kvernadze, Gabriele Bracaglia and goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani.

It has been revealed that frosinone won 3-0 at Fiorentina, beat Cesc Fabregas’s Como 2-0 and Torino by the same score. At Atalanta – the Europa League winners of 2024 now managed by Sarri – they drew 4-4 and came within a whisker of a late winner.

Twenty points from the first ten games recalled the early bursts of Claudio Ranieri’s newly promoted Fiorentina in 1994-95 and Juventus in 2007-08.

Then, in the last fixture before the international break, came a third defeat of the season, at home against Cagliari, despite 29 shots and 13 corners. One of those days when the ball simply refused to go in.

It has been revealed that whether the shareholders of Clara Vista – which bought 80 per cent of Frosinone in the summer – are entirely delighted remains to be seen. There have been suggestions they hoped to see more of the 13 players signed via their data algorithms but only Patrizio Masini and Romano Schmid have been regular starters.

The other nine or 10 names regularly in the starting XI are the same men who drove the climb out of Serie B.

Defensive midfielder Giacomo Calo has scored five goals in 11 games this season.

When it comes to the metric of ‘passes per defensive action’, a key indicator of how promptly the ball is won back, Frosinone rank among the top four clubs in Europe. The others are Barcelona, Brighton and De Zerbi’s Tottenham.

In a recent development, still, Alvini shrugs off the praise. His first seven years as a coach produced two promotions, one sacking and one relegation. Then a group of friends decided to start a club in the seventh tier (the third amateur level) and put him in charge.

In the seven seasons from 2008 to 2015, Tuttocuoio climbed via four promotions into Serie C.

Sources indicate that alvini moved on to fresh challenges. The next four seasons at Pistoiese and AlbinoLeffe brought his first two professional sackings. He lists them openly on LinkedIn, almost as badges of honour, albeit the second was not a conventional dismissal.

Emergency surgery to insert an artery stent early in the season left him psychologically raw when he returned.

Those three years at AlbinoLeffe however proved formative because he was able to watch Gian Piero Gasperini’s Atalanta methods at close quarters. He took that inspiration into the following campaign at Reggiana, taking them back to Serie B after 21 years for his seventh promotion.

Industry observers note that frosinone supplied the eighth and his second taste of Serie A. The first came when he was tempted from Perguia to Cremonese with a team simply not equipped for a relegation scrap. He was sacked by January.

The return is proving sweeter than he could have dared to imagine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Sources indicate that enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#94573. Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.
  • Recent findings suggest that four of the Substantial Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools.
  • Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Substantial Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.

Recent findings suggest that four of the Substantial Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools. They have sold a further €37 billion ($41 billion) of bonds in euros.

Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Substantial Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.

Next year, Goldman Sachs projects that total new AI hyperscaler bond sales are expected to reach $420 billion. About €60 billion will be issued in euros, according to Dutch bank ING.

That is unwelcome news for European companies and countries like France, Germany and Italy, whose sovereign bond yields have risen sharply in recent months and are already straining public finances.

With public debt at 119% of gross domestic product (GDP) and a deficit still running above 5%, France is already paying a sizable risk premium on its debt. Over the past six months, yields on French 10-year bonds have climbed from roughly 3.7% to nearly 5%.

The French government's interest bill is set to rise from €79 billion right now to €91 billion next year and over €100 billion by 2028.

Based on these figures alone, France's Finance Ministry needs to find tens of billions of euros in additional cuts, tax hikes, or more borrowing by the end of the decade.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In August, economists at the European Central Bank remarked the euro bond market was adapting well to the presence of AI giants but warned they "could make it harder for other companies and other economic sectors to access finance.".

Writing in a blog post, they also questioned whether the bloc's financial markets can "smoothly handle such large and concentrated debt inflows and warned of a "potential spillover to the sovereign and supranational segment of the bond market.".

That means governments and international lenders such as the European Union and the European Investment Bank could also end up paying more to borrow.

Viktor Hjort, global head of credit strategy at the French bank BNP Paribas, described the phenomenon as "bond abundance.".

Hjort told DW that the presence of the hyperscalers in the euro bond market is "already high enough to create competition" within the corporate sector and "between corporates and governments for available fixed income funds." These are investment funds that mostly buy bonds, which pay regular interest.

Bond yields jumped again last month, driven by rebounding energy prices linked to the Iran war and France’s political crisis, which Hjort remarked further revealed the growing competition for capital, as government and organization borrowing costs rose together.

Normally, nervous investors move into government bonds during uncertain times, which pushes their borrowing costs down.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Goldman Sachs warned last week that rising interest costs were starting to hurt earnings at European companies. Among firms in the Stoxx 600 — an index of 600 large, mid-sized and small companies across Europe — Goldman found that interest costs as a share of sales have risen by nearly half since 2022.

The bank's analysts mentioned this had cut earnings by more than 5% over the same period.

Factor in the competition from AI bonds, and European firms could now face pressure to cut their investments in new plants, equipment and research, as well as shareholder payouts, to prioritize loan repayments.

The pressure doesn't stop at national governments. Europe's cities and regions, whose borrowing helps to fund schools, transport and infrastructure, may also feel the effects of the AI boom.

A study for the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development(OECD), published in January, compared local bond markets in Belgium, Germany, Spain, Sweden and Canada. Where AI was spreading fastest, measured by the share of AI-related job vacancies, borrowing costs for cities and regions tended to rise.

"Whereas in the United States, my research has found that AI investments are linked to a lower cost of borrowing for municipalities, the opposite appears to hold in several European countries," the study's co-author, Christos Makridis of Arizona State University's W. P. Carey School of Business, told DW.

While AI bonds are far from the sole cause of Europe's widening fiscal strains, US Big Tech's huge appetite for capital could add further pressure next year, due to the additional billions in latest bonds planned.

The irony is that European taxpayers could end up paying more on their own governments' debt, partly to help finance an AI boom across the Atlantic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 06:20 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:30 EST, 21 November 2026.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been seen in public for the first time since the tragic accident.

During a match earlier this month, Andorra keeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out Tenerife star de Miguel with a high challenge which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

De Miguel's passing shocked the footballing world and Owono was subsequently given a 12-match ban by authorities.

Both sides have been back in action since the tragedy, but on Friday, Andorra hosted Leganes at their Estadi de la FAF.

That was their first home game since de Miguel's passing, and they made sure to pay a moving tribute to him on the night.

Before the match, the players went onto the pitch wearing shirts with his name and number on them and they carried out a bouquet of white flowers.

Andorra keeper Jesus Owono was seen in public for the first time since Jesus de Miguel's tragic death as he attended a tribute to the former Tenerife star.

Before Andorra's game with Legannes, several tributes were paid, including a minute's silence.

A minute's silence was also held before the game, while those in attendance applauded during the ninth minute of the match, the shirt number worn by de Miguel at Tenerife.

The most striking part of the evening though was Owono's attendance in the stands.

The goalkeeper has stayed away from the public eye since de Miguel's death, after which he was subjected to chants of 'murderer', but he wanted to attend the tribute at his club's home ground.

Owono was wearing a black coat and hat as he stood next to team-mates who weren't involved in the matchday squad.

Despite receiving the support of the crowd and his team-mates, local reports mentioned Owono cut a downcast figure and that he was seen praying immediately after the minute's silence.

Owono's desire to attend the tribute came after he had also asked to meet de Miguel's family, something he hopes to do one day.

Meanwhile, Tenerife returned to action last week against AD Ceuta CF in a match that was also filled with tributes.

Players provided a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – another nod to de Miguel's shirt number.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars then took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the tragedy.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of de Miguel before the game kicked off.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

In a recent development, other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, de Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place de Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

Owono was watching the game from the stands as he stood next to some of his team-mates.

Tenerife returned to action last week and paid several tributes to their former star de Miguel.

The tragedy occurred as the game between Tenerife and Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when de Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for his side in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, de Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

Owono's 12-match ban is at the moment in effect, yet his manager Carles Manso hinted that he may never play again.

He said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A little over two months before it was set to kick off, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed its flagship international football tournament in the wake of recent deadly attacks on host country, Saudi Arabia.

The AFC cited "substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions" caused by conflicts in the region.

Instead of January 7, 2027, the tournament will now kick off on December 23 and end on January 21, 2028. The postponement follows delays and cancellations of a number of sporting events in the region, including a Formula One race, the men's and women's tennis finals, the 2027 Dakar Rally and disruption to Asia's marquee continental club football tournament, the AFC Champions League Elite.

Saudi Arabia hosted, and won, the Gulf Cup last month, but there had already been much talk about whether the much larger Asian Cup could go ahead.

Recent findings suggest that it was scheduled to feature 24 teams playing matches in eight venues across Riyadh, Jeddah and Khobar. However, the AFC stated that "circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions," made the tournament impossible.

"Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organization and delivery of the competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.".

Industry observers note that in particular, the postponement was forced by a recent wave of deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi rebels as well as other raging conflicts in the region. The Houthis have targeted Saudi infrastructure, including airports. They are fighting a Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognized government, a civil war that reignited in July following a years-long truce.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The AFC had been under pressure from several federations to postpone the tournament, with South Korea's players leading the way.

"The ongoing military tensions and security instability in the Middle East are complications that cannot be taken lightly," Lee Keun-ho, president of the Korea Professional Footballers Association, noted last month, according to the Yonhap News Agency.

Lee added that "no tournament's value can take precedence over the lives and safety of players and football fans.".

In a recent development, it seems that the AFC now agrees. However, following the announcement of the postponement, Yasser al-Misehal, chairman of the local organizing committee, promised that Saudi Arabia was "fully ready" whenever the tournament ended up being held.

"The tournament will move to the new dates, and our preparations will continue as planned," he told the Saudi Press Agency.

"We're working closely with the AFC and all our partners to make sure the tournament runs smoothly and meets the high standards expected of Saudi Arabia and the Asian Cup.".

Saudi Arabia has invested hugely in sports over the last decade, from owning Premier League teams to hosting boxing title fights and bidding for a number of major sporting events, most notably World Cup 2034, which they won the right to host unopposed.

However, the country has recently withdrawn or slashed funding for a number of sporting events including golf, rugby, tennis and winter sports.

Latest Update: Meet ‘egoviruses’: the surprise microbes living in the guts of millions of people

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (729 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Many giant viruses can be seen under a light microscope.Credit: Gabrielle Voinot/Eurelios/Look at Sciences/SPL.
  • Roughly 180 million people could be carrying previously unknown giant viruses inside their guts.
  • Large and giant viruses in the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are a vast group of DNA viruses — some are so big that they can be seen under a light microscope — that mostly infect single-celled organisms in the environment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many giant viruses can be seen under a light microscope.Credit: Gabrielle Voinot/Eurelios/Look at Sciences/SPL.

Roughly 180 million people could be carrying previously unknown giant viruses inside their guts. Microbiologists say that these ‘egoviruses’ could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly. The findings are published in Nature1.

Large and giant viruses in the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are a vast group of DNA viruses — some are so big that they can be seen under a light microscope — that mostly infect single-celled organisms in the environment.

Poxviruses are an outlier in the giant-virus world because they can directly infect humans and animals and their origin is a mystery, indicates Fasséli Coulibaly, a structural biologist at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia. Egoviruses could be the evolutionary bridge between microorganism-infecting giant viruses called asfuviruses and pathogenic poxviruses, he says.

Tom Delmont, a microbial ecologist at the French National Centre for Scientific Research in Paris, and his colleagues discovered egoviruses while combing through online libraries of metagenomes. These contain the genetic information of all the organisms in a particular environment, which means that researchers can hunt for microbes without having to cultivate them. When the team scanned for a single gene found in most nucleocytoviruses, they discovered egoviruses — the only type of nucleocytovirus that is prevalent in the gut.

They found egovirus DNA in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people. One of these clades is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the global population, on the basis of the presence of at least one of two egovirus proteins in the samples they analysed.

The researchers detected these proteins in samples spanning a large proportion of the human population, from the Hadza, a hunter-gatherer group in Tanzania, to populations in Europe, the United States and South America, says Delmont. That suggests that egoviruses have been inhabiting the human gut for a long time, he adds.

In a recent development, that egoviruses are found in many animal species, including people, and are widespread around the world shows that giant viruses are more diverse than previously thought, indicates Subir Sarker, a molecular virologist at James Cook University in Townsville, Queensland. “This is a really groundbreaking study,” he adds.

Sources indicate that to identify potential hosts for egoviruses in the gut, the team compared the amount of genetic overlap between egoviruses and organisms with a nucleus. The researchers found the most overlap with single-celled organisms that help ruminants, such as cows, to digest their food.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03766-w.

In a recent development, “Captain Underpants”. The laughter that follows is infectious. It seems doubtful that it was an honest answer to the question posed to Zach Lee by the young boy located somewhere near the front of the classroom: “What is your favourite book?” But it got exactly the reaction he was after.

Recent findings suggest that the room is abuzz. It has been for much of the past hour.

Sources indicate that goalkeeper Lee and five of his Everton Under-21s teammates have gleefully taken up the task of being reading buddies to the children of Ellesmere Port’s Meadow Primary School, one of six schools that make up the recently renamed Everton Multi-Academy Trust (EMAT). Seven miles away, six of their Under-21 peers are doing likewise at Oldfield Primary School in Chester.

Nearer to Liverpool, the hollers that greeted Everton Women’s Holly McNamara and Karen Holmgaard 24 hours earlier are still reverberating around the corridors of Bidston Avenue Primary School.

Christian Nørgaard and close friends Tyler Dibling and Tyrique George are also familiar with the noise the pupils at the Birkenhead school can make. Last month, the trio were serenaded with a ukulele rendition of Spirit of the Blues on a visit there. Blue ukuleles, of course.

If the colour of the musical instruments is a cute indicator of the strengthening ties between the football club and the EMAT schools, the time being spared by the players is of much greater significance.

It is intended to demonstrate a cross-Club connection with EMAT, which sits alongside Everton in the Community as one of Everton’s associated organisations. “Part of the Everton family,” as Everton’s Chief Tax and Sustainability Officer and Chair of Trustees for EMAT Alison Haynes puts it.

In a recent development, but there is a deeper intention, too. “We want to use the power of the Everton crest to inspire and engage youngsters in education,” states Steven Baker OBE, CEO of EMAT. Baker has seen this in evidence for more than a decade, having previously served as Principal of Everton Alternative Provision Free School, the award-winning L4 facility that offers youngsters who have struggled in mainstream schools a route back into education.

Lee and his Under-21 colleagues, McNamara and Holmgaard are all supporting one particular mission of EMAT - to inspire youngsters towards a life-long love of reading. More immediately, to ensure they have the requisite literacy level to adequately prepare them for what lies ahead in secondary school education.

Sources indicate that in Ellesmere Port, Chester and Birkenhead, the players are tackling their role head on. Books - donated by Everton staff to help replenish the schools’ libraries - are strewn across the tables and spilling onto the floor. No-one’s troubled by the mess.

It has been revealed that julia Donaldson’s greatest hits are being played out across the room. Michael Morpurgo – a childhood favourite author of midfielder Jack Patterson – can be heard, too. ‘Bluey’ is an appropriately named hit on another table. And then there’s Lee and a group of little ones giggling at Captain Underpants.

Close by to the classroom at Meadow, Everton’s leading post-war goalscorer Graeme Sharp is here too, continuing the literacy theme by officially opening the school’s newly-refurbished library.

According to recent reports, “These children will remember today,” notes Baker. “They will remember players from Everton coming into school and taking the time to sit with them.

According to recent reports, “They love hearing stories but they also love having someone to read to. Both aspects are so important for a child’s development.”.

Recent findings suggest that as is music. It’s why Dibling, George and Norgaard found themselves being taught the chords to one of Goodison’s – and now Hill Dickinson Stadium’s – favourite tunes last month.

Studies show a direct correlation between a child mastering a musical instrument and making their mark in maths and other creative fields.

The Toffees trio left behind gifts of recorders (blue ones), helping the school expand the opportunities it can offer to its pupils.

“We find it’s really notable for their resilience and it's good for the children mentally and socially to have the opportunity to not only play an instrument, but to play to an audience,” says Bidston Avenue headteacher Stuart Brady, a Tranmere Rovers fan.

“It's great for us as a school to have the connection we do with Everton and the players. Days like this are great, but it's also about the children feeling they belong to something bigger.”.

It has been revealed that and the proof that EMAT is getting it right is stacking up. In 2024, Everton Free School and Everton Football College – the two original schools on which the Trust was founded – were jointly awarded an ‘Outstanding’ rating by Ofsted. Earlier this year, the respected national TES Awards named EMAT (then The People’s Learning Trust) as its Trust of the Year for trusts with nine schools or fewer.

With the support of a Premier League football club and its players behind them, it is hoped the collective will continue to go from strength to strength.

Recent findings suggest that the intention is that Everton’s Under-21s will return to the schools to resume their reading buddy duties at junctures throughout the season, strengthening their bonds with the schools and pupils. It is seen as a vital part of the players’ professional development.

Industry observers note that representatives from the Men’s and Women’s team will continue to play their part also. Merlin Röhl has already been a guest of Oldfield Primary School’s after-school chess club, taking up an invitation to share his love of the ancient game with the next generation.

“We understand the responsibility and influence we have as a football club when it comes to our communities,” says Haynes. “And you cannot understate the impact the player visits have.

“The atmosphere and the smiles you see in the room, the energy they give to the children… it’s truly wonderful.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that de Miguel was involved in a clash in the middle of the pitch with FC Andorra's Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball with the score 2-2 late in the game.
  • According to recent reports, spanish media reported that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Heartbroken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real." Those were the words with which Spanish second division football club Tenerife confirmed the death of 30-year-old Jesus de Miguel on Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that de Miguel was involved in a clash in the middle of the pitch with FC Andorra's Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball with the score 2-2 late in the game. Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.

According to recent reports, spanish media reported that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically" before his death.

After confirming the death on Tuesday morning, the club posted that: "No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news.".

Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" as messages of support began to flood in on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that "I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media.

Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish FA (RFEF).

"Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today," wrote the federation in a statement.

The RFEF postponed Tuesday's matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina, "as a gesture of respect and solidarity.".

De Miguel had been with Tenerife since joining from from Castellon in 2025. He began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023.

How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (773 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.
  • Recent findings suggest that it is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture.
  • Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.

Recent findings suggest that it is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture. The asterisk signals the inclusion of non-Arab ethnic minorities and people with diverse identities and roots in Southwest Asia and North Africa.

Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.

This year's theme, "Who's Your Diva?!," brought together drag performers paying tribute to legendary figures from across the Eastern Mediterranean who have become queer icons — from Egyptian music legend Umm Kulthum to Turkish star Bülent Ersoy and Lebanese pop icon Haifa Wehbe.

Hassandra, co-founder of ADIRA and the ADIRA Drag Festival, was among the performers, taking on the persona of Lebanese pop star Elissa.

"It is very important for me to bring my Lebanese Arab identity and culture into what I do, because I think it's a very beautiful culture. And there's a lot of campy, glamorous, beautiful divas," Hassandra stated.

In a recent development, elissa's "whole discography is very romantic, raw, soft, kind of like very Adele vibes," Hassandra told DW ahead of the October 30 show. "However, her personality is known to be the extreme opposite. She's very feisty. Very blunt, very unfiltered. Not soft at all as a person.".

Sources indicate that the star is also known for speaking out on political challenges in Lebanon. She has publicly voiced support for LGBTQ+ communities in the Middle East, while also frequently sparking controversy across the Arab world with her outspoken positions on other political issues.

Hassandra's ADIRA Drag Festival performance addresses this complexity, ultimately "tapping into her sort of controversial political opinions," the drag artist explained.

This reflects one of the ideas Hassandra hopes to promote with the theme of this year's festival. "As queer people, we tend to idealize a lot of pop divas. But these pop divas are very imperfect in their nature," Hassandra said. The show provides an opportunity to critically revisit these divas' legacy through a more critical lens.

"And this sort of critical lens can be taken into the outside world, as in: never follow anyone in life blindly. No one should follow any politician, any political party, any pop diva, any activist blindly.".

Born in Beirut in 1994, Hassandra studied theater and stage acting at the Lebanese University before moving to Berlin in 2017. "I would say it was it was just a very sort of impulsive decision at the age of 22. I mean, there's no doubt that the economic situation was really bad in Lebanon and continued to become even worse," the artist said.

In Berlin, Hassandra became increasingly involved in the city's independent art scene and queer nightlife. Drag emerged as another form of self-expression for the actor.

Through performances that combine theatrical intensity, political humor, grotesque aesthetics and moments of tenderness, Hassandra challenges conventional understandings of gender and identity.

Their work explores themes of home, nostalgia, displacement and queer Arab culture. These ideas are also central to ADIRA, which Hassandra founded in 2023 with Syrian-German DJ and cultural producer Zuher Jazmati, also known as xanax_attax.

Through panel discussions, performances and music events, ADIRA fosters collective participation and community-building.

As Islamophobia and homophobia rise alongside the far right, spaces like ADIRA offer a sense of belonging and support for Arab queer communities.

That sense of community has become even more crucial following the deadly Islamist terrorist attack during Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride parade in July.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that in the aftermath, Hassandra felt caught between their different identities. As an Arab queer person, "you fall in this position where then you start receiving a lot of racism," they noted.

"And I think this is why it's important, for us queer Arabs, to say we are sad over what happened, but that we also reject any of the racism that comes from that," Hassandra said. "I think we [the Arab community] are being used in a lot of ways as a punching bag for a lot of things that are happening.".

In a recent development, rather than allowing the attack to fuel hatred and racism, Hassandra said, "we should make Germany a safer place for everyone to live in."  "There's place for everyone. It's a huge country," they added.

Welsh Rugby Union's 20,000 reasons to be ashamed.

In a recent development, among the joys of this job is being present at rare moments of sporting greatness. The Welsh win over the All Blacks last weekend was one such occasion and, for me, it was compounded by a subsequent email from a lovely chap named John Evans, aged 87 and from Tredegar in Blaenau Gwent.

John had watched the game on television, but was part of what must be a dwindling group who could say they were there the last time Wales had beaten Latest Zealand, at the Arms Park in 1953.

After detailing how he, ‘a small-bottomed outside-half’, had left himself with no view of the pitch at the back of the stand, John went on to recall that the crowd around him and a friend ‘decided to pass us over everyone’s head back down to the front’. He landed just in time to see Ken Jones score the winning try. His excitement in sharing a memory from 73 years ago was spelled out in block capitals.

One of the consequences of the ongoing shambles at the Welsh Rugby Union is that there were 20,000 empty seats at the Principality Stadium last weekend, mainly due to a combination of apathy and protest. Accordingly, there will be 20,000 fewer people with a great story to tell decades from now. While the WRU ponder their next blunders, they might wish to consider some of the above.

According to recent reports, from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, noted of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

It has been revealed that “I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

In a recent development, some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

Industry observers note that this is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

In a recent development, this is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Recent findings suggest that arteta mentioned: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes mentioned: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

According to recent reports, “When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Gennaro Gattuso expressed his ‘pride’ as Lazio swept Lecce aside 3-0 to stay top of the Serie A table. ‘I don’t mind misplaced passes, because we play at such a high tempo.’.

The Aquile will spend at least another week on top of the Serie A table following today’s 3-0 victory over Cagliari at the Stadio Olimpico.

Tijjani Noslin found the net twice before Davide Frattesi put the cherry on top with a delightful lob in the final minutes of the match.

“I am proud of the mentality and the hunger shown by the team today,” Gattuso told DAZN Italia.

“We didn’t have the best start, but then got control of the game, both in possession and off the ball. Lecce are an uncomfortable opponent, they always come and push you, so it is fundamental for us to keep this attitude.”.

There is always some concern for coaches after the break for international duty, but Gattuso assures he had no such qualms about his Lazio players.

According to recent reports, “I saw the way they were training, so I was not worried. There is a great spirit and application, we’ve got to keep going like this. It is all down to the players, they are putting in the right mentality, hunger and sense of belonging. They are doing something incredible.”.

Lazio are top of the table and still unbeaten in Serie A despite a lot of injury problems, as today they were missing Mattia Zaccagni, Nuno Tavares, Josip Sutalo and Adam Marusic.

Nicolò Rovella also came off the bench late on and is still trying to work his way back to full fitness after numerous issues.

“Rovella can give us more vertical passes, as when he gets the ball, he immediately looks up and forward,” explained the coach.

According to recent reports, “I think we also need to talk about Fisayo Dele-Bashiru. He deserves more. We’ve got to give Rovella playing time so that he can regain fitness, then he can give us an crucial hand.”.

Considering how well Lazio are doing under Gattuso so far this season, is there anything he still hasn’t seen and wants them to improve?

Sources indicate that “I don’t mind losing the ball with misplaced passes that much, because when you play at a high tempo, that can happen. I am more interested in the mentality of the side and how they are hanging in there under pressure.

“I am satisfied, you always want something more, but at this tempo there are going to be some misplaced passes. We can improve our reading of the game, as for example today when we struggled to get through the middle, we needed to spread the game out wide.”.
