Industry observers note that mcTominay remains open to staying in Naples, but discussions over an extension have stalled. Chelsea, AC Milan and Juventus are also monitoring developments, while clubs from Saudi Arabia have shown interest.

A return to Old Trafford would be particularly interesting following Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, with United expected to reshape their midfield in 2027.

United sold McTominay at a point when he was often viewed as a useful squad player rather than a guaranteed starter.

That perception has changed dramatically. A recent CaughtOffside report highlighted how his performances in Italy have turned him into a much more complete midfielder, capable of contributing both defensively and in the final third.

According to recent reports, that profile could appeal to Pochettino. McTominay already understands the club, the league and the pressure surrounding United, meaning there would be virtually no adaptation period. His goalscoring ability from midfield could also become particularly valuable if Bruno Fernandes eventually leaves.

The obvious concern is price. United would effectively be paying to re-sign a player they sold for far less only a few years earlier, which would inevitably invite criticism.

But recruitment decisions should be judged on the player United would be buying now, not the one they sold in 2024.

If Napoli’s contract talks continue to stall and the fee becomes reasonable, a McTominay return should be taken seriously. He left Old Trafford as a useful midfielder, he could return as a considerably better one.

Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

The 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

Industry observers note that the trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

It has been revealed that half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

According to recent reports, in the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, said Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

Industry observers note that exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a fresh cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

In cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

Recent findings suggest that eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that for people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

According to recent reports, in another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

It has been revealed that even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

Earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

Industry observers note that "I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she remarked. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

In a recent development, nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he stated.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell said that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she said.

In a recent development, nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he stated.

Recent findings suggest that he is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

In a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

"There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," said Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

According to recent reports, campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she remarked, if run by properly trained staff.

Sources indicate that one recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she said.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

In a recent development, according to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and manufacturer. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives. The big-brained, tool-wielding species emerged two million years ago in Africa and expanded across Eurasia, before vanishing around 100,000 years ago in Java, Indonesia.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

In a recent development, did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Sources indicate that researchers have now added another feather to the hominin’s cap. A pair of studies analysing fossil teeth1,2, which were published in Nature on 18 November, suggest that H. erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.

Recent findings suggest that researchers had thought that H. erectus was limited to savannahs and open woodlands, notes Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, and a co-author of both studies.

“Never, ever have we seen them in rainforests,” she adds. “This is a really major deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

It has been revealed that the earliest H. erectus fossils, from eastern Africa, are 1.9 million years old. But the svelte, upright-walking and running hominins wasted little time, reaching western Asia and present-day China some 200,000 years later and modern Java, using land bridges, not long after. The last-known H. erectus remains, from central Java, date to roughly 110,000 years ago3.

Limestone caves in Guangxi province, southern China, contained more than 10,000 fossil teeth.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

It has been revealed that while looking for fossils from a three-metre-tall great ape called Gigantopithecus, Westaway and her colleagues identified a pair of limestone caves in Guangxi province in southern China. There, they discovered more than 10,000 fossil teeth from animals such as orangutans (Pongo spp.), monkeys and wild boar (Sus spp.), as well as 9 from hominins. The researchers estimate that the hominins lived between 184,000 and 324,000 years ago, according to dating of both fossils and the surrounding sediments using various methods.

Eight of the hominin teeth resembled those of H. erectus in their shape, a designation that was confirmed by analysing the sequences of proteins preserved in the dental enamel of four specimens, indicates co-author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen.

The tooth enamel was analysed and its proteins sequenced.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

The ninth lacked the shape and protein signature of H. erectus teeth, says Welker, and it also didn’t resemble those of H. sapiens or Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis). Denisovans — enigmatic ancient humans first discovered in southern Siberia and now linked to diverse fossils from China and elsewhere in Asia — are a possibility, but the evidence is circumstantial, says Welker. “Every label we put on that ninth tooth is a little bit of speculation.”.

The multitude of animal teeth was probably accumulated by a scavenger such as a porcupine. The presence of fossils from species such as muntjac deer (Muntiacus muntjac), leopards and orangutans hints at a rainforest environment.

Newcastle United hosted Arsenal in the Premier League on Saturday evening, and fans were not happy about the state of the team even before a ball was kicked.

The Magpies started with a team that looked very weak on paper, including young midfielders Seun Steur and Lewis Miley playing, with Joe Willock in midfield, and Jacob Murphy in attack alongside William Osula and Harvey Barnes.

The substitutes' bench saw much stronger options available, including the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Anthony Elanga, Nico Gonzalez, Yoanne Wissa, Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey, and Sven Botman.

But perhaps more significantly was the fact that two summer signings in Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure were not included in the matchday squad at all by Matthias Jaissle, despite the club spending £72m on the pair under Eddie Howe.

Neither player was expected to be ready to make an immediate impact on the starting lineup this season considering their age, profile, and experience at the top level. But to not be included in the squad at all, despite the clear complications that the squad is having this season, suggests that the manager has no faith in their qualities.

Industry observers note that it's also worth noting that Newcastle were without Joelinton for the game, with the Brazilian injured and unavailable for selection. That would imply that both players are even further down the pecking order than it may seem initially.

Sources indicate that bamba's lack of involvement is potentially not as worrying, because of the options in midfield. Steur has been pushing for an opportunity, and with Nico Gonzalez on the bench, and Jaissle a huge fan of Willock, him being left out on this occasion can be excused.

But for Toure, the situation is hugely different. Newcastle have been struggling for goals all season, managing just 13 goals in their 10 games before the Arsenal fixture, and their top scorers Barnes, Willock, and Elanga all have just two goals each.

Recent findings suggest that other attacking options in the squad have struggled to make any sort of impact too, while Toure has two goals this season despite having started just one game in all competitions. His incredible pace, dribbling ability, and creativity should mean that he should at least be considered by a manager looking for ways to turn the team's fortunes around.

When Newcastle agreed a £42m deal to sign Toure from Hoffenheim, it was with the idea of him becoming an integral part of the future of the club under Eddie Howe.

But before the season even began Howe had left, and it now looks evident that Toure is not someone that Jaissle wants as part of his squad.

The Ivorian hasn't started a game since August, and despite the team winning just three of their opening ten games in the Premier League, he can't get a look in. Jaissle has no interest in giving Toure an opportunity at this point, and his exclusion from the squad against Arsenal proves it.

If Newcastle had known that Jaissle was going to come in and not be a fan of Toure, then there is no way they would have committed such a large fee to bringing him into the club just to be sidelined. It's a huge oversight on behalf of the board, and it's a massive waste of money too.

According to Opta, the only other Giallorossi player to score more than 25 league goals in a calendar year is Pedro Manfredini, who also scored 26 in 1960. With six weeks of the year still to go, Malen needs one more goal to become the first Roma player to reach 27.

Malen’s tally also puts him ahead of some of Europe’s top strikers this year. TuttoMercatoWeb point out that Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane, the reigning Ballon d’Or winner, and Barcelona’s Raphinha have 21 league goals each in 2026. Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé has 19 in La Liga. The comparison covers league goals only, so cup and international matches aren’t included.

The Dutchman scored 14 of his 26 in the second half of last season after joining from Aston Villa. He has 12 in 11 games this season, which makes him Serie A’s top scorer, three ahead of Monza’s Gustavo Varela.

In a recent development, he’ll turn 28 in January and has found consistency as a central striker that he never quite had in England. Roma are now working on a new contract for him, although his current deal already runs until 2030.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer.
  • The idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate.
  • "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time.

The idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.

"This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating.".

Previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception.

Sources indicate that under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the new format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees powerhouses the US and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.

Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria.

Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark.

Sources indicate that no. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

As noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament — and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada with five, USA with three) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February.

Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a world championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milan.

The United States and Canada will play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute.

In a recent development, the Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, remarked in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.

"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice," Hockey Canada remarked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Sources indicate that eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

According to recent reports, “You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”.

This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”.

A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM.

Industry observers note that the precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

So while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

According to recent reports, the anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Recent findings suggest that arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”.

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

It was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

Recent findings suggest that salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

FLEETWOOD TAKE THE LEAD! 😱 Loupalo-Bi puts League Two side Fleetwood ahead against Arsenal 💥 https://t.co/zTFEkCp0oL.

Industry observers note that as the home fans set off flares, filling the air with plumes of thick, red smoke, the theme tune to Captain Pugwash was played. Arteta tried to find answers from his coaching staff, amid the cacophony, but occasionally you do not have to look too deep for answers.

It has been revealed that could the miracle happen? When half-time arrived with Fleetwood still in the lead, you began to wonder. But then you saw Ben White and Martin Odegaard go through intense warm-ups so they could be introduced at the start of the second half and you knew the mountain had become taller.

So it proved. Odegaard, with his mesmerising left foot and all-encompassing vision, did more in the first five minutes of the second period than many of his colleagues had managed before the interval, and Arsenal levelled in that initial flurry through Gyökeres’s first domestic goal of the campaign.

Viktor Gyökeres gets his first goal of the season and Arsenal are level against Fleetwood! 🔴 https://t.co/LfZcIbAfCX.

In a recent development, A game of attack against defence played out for the remainder before Dowman was harshly dismissed in the 85th minute after reacting to a tough challenge from Neal. There was still time for Fleetwood’s Lynch to make two excellent saves from White and Odegaard in added time as Arsenal tried to avoid the shoot-out lottery. They could not and how it hurt them.

HUGE save from Jay Lynch! https://t.co/dLJaFwCmHQ.

“Football’s getting a little bit more, I don’t know, clinical and removed,” Matt Lawlor, the Fleetwood manager, said. “To me, there was that feeling we all get as football fans. That was what you kind of live for, isn’t it? To be a part of it is special.

Sources indicate that “To be giving that to football fans and especially Fleetwood fans is unbelievably special. I’m really proud of it. Football’s a funny old game, isn’t it?”.

First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through in the next round, in the manner they’ve done it, the atmosphere they have created, and, yeah, a really sad day for us.

I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players. I haven’t seen anyone not doing what is required at this level. But, obviously, we insisted so much, we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, obviously, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. And football is about that.

Sources indicate that attitude wise, absolutely zero [wrong] otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way. It had nothing to do with effort or application or determination to win it, but we lack other things to, to create a much bigger margin than today, with what we produce, they really should have been shown in the scoreline.

Something that we discussed already before the match.

It’s difficult to see on the cameras, I prefer to watch it back properly and I will assess the situation.

We will learn from everything [on if he will learn from it].

Industry observers note that I don’t think it will [sink in], it’s really hard to address the players when we have a league game on Saturday and I didn’t want to be the bearer of reality. The biggest night in the club’s history. We’ve beaten the champions, somehow!

It has been revealed that we knew before the game, we’re not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we’re going to go to the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country and the best of the basics and the world-class players, in that we’re going to go and outplay them. So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game.

Obviously, the goal happens, but they’re going to happen; they’re so good at football. The footballers that they have, the gaps that they find and we see it every week in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that to beat the English champions on penalties, credit to everyone one of these lads. We looked at Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We compared it even though these are the champions. We thought ‘if we lay it all out there, let’s see what happens.

Luca Williams-Barnett took all the headlines as he scored the opening goal and then set up Dominic Solanke for the second, helping the Lilywhites to their fourth win in five games in the top flight.

The youngster was handed his first start for the club, as Roberto De Zerbi admitted that a number of factors had led to the decision, and also contributed to a number of other changes being made to the starting lineup for the clash.

Sandro Tonali missed out due to illness, while Mathys Tel has been ruled out until next month with an ankle injury. Destiny Udogie, Conor Gallagher, James Maddison, and Solanke all also earned starts after missing out last time, with Andy Robertson, Archie Gray, Omar Marmoush, Tel and Tonali all dropping out.

But there was a more unexpected change in the defence for the game too, with Marcos Senesi coming in alongside Jan Paul van Hecke, with Micky Van de Ven dropping to the bench.

Van de Ven played 90 minutes in both of the Netherlands fixtures during the international break, as they claimed a 7-0 win over Greece before being crushed 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp's Germany, but despite being fit and available, he was left out against the Tractor Boys.

Spurs didn't miss him in the slightest, however, as the Argentina international stepped into the side and turned in a brilliant performance to help unlock the low block of Gary O'Neil's side with his excellent passing out from the back and reading of the game.

It was the third time this season that Van Hecke and Senesi have started together, and it was their first win, having previously played in the 3-0 defeat to Brentford on the opening day, and the 1-1 draw against Man Utd at Old Trafford.

But the draw against United should have been a comfortable win but for some poor finishing from the forwards, and this performance against Ipswich was among the best the team have had this season. It's no coincidence that the control of the team was far more stable with Senesi in the side, and it now looks like he should be keeping his place in the team.

With the way that De Zerbi wants to play, control is paramount. Van de Ven is a top defender, and the club clearly rates him highly after handing him a bumper new contract in the summer.

But Senesi has shown, whenever he has played, that he is more of a fit for the manager's prepares and style, and that is now leading to an uncomfortable conversation about him being in the team ahead of the captain.

If the manager is serious about creating an environment and atmosphere in the squad that is competitive, then he shouldn't be afraid to drop big names when he has other players who are outperforming them.

It has been revealed that if Van de Ven is the leader that the club see him as, then he should react to the decision to leave him out by stepping up in training and being ready to claim his place back. Senesi deserves his spot in the side, and his performance proves it. Now it's on De Zerbi to make the decision to actually pull the trigger.

Latest Update: Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • Sources indicate that it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

Sources indicate that it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

The first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

Recent findings suggest that since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that at that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, said additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

"Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler remarked. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

In a recent development, "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," noted Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," mentioned BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

According to recent reports, this year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," remarked Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," stated Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

Aston Villa were held to a 0-0 draw against relegation-battling Sunderland on Saturday afternoon, as Unai Emery's side continued their mixed start to the campaign.

The Villans have won just three of their first 11 games in the Premier League this season after the result at Villa Park, leaving them in 11th place in the table, despite having seen the majority of their starting lineup depart during the summer transfer window.

Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea, Youri Tielemans joined Man Utd, Lucas Digne joined Paris Saint-Germain, Ezri Konsa joined Arsenal, Ollie Watkins joined Al-Hilal, and Emi Martinez joined Chelsea, leaving Emery incredibly short of experience and familiarity within his squad.

Emery brought in 10 new players during the summer window to help replace them and strengthen the squad, but the team have struggled to adapt and the results have not been as forthcoming as they would have hoped.

But while Konsa has gone from strength to strength since his move to the Emirates Stadium, establishing himself as one of the best central defenders in the Premier League, the lack of goals in the side has been more of a problem.

Watkins' departure has left a major hole in the side, and while Nicolas Jackson's performances have been largely good, that reliable threat of scoring regularly seems to have gone.

But what is not being spoken about enough is the fact that Aston Villa also allowed Donyell Malen to leave the club permanently in the summer, and he would be the perfect solution to a lot of the issues they are presently having.

The Netherlands international has been in remarkable form since joining AS Roma on an initial loan deal in the January transfer window, scoring 25 goals in Serie A - 12 more than the next-best players in Marcus Thuram and Anastasios Douvikas.

The forward extended his place at the top of that chart with a stunning performance on Saturday night as he scored four goals in their win over Parma, and revealed Aston Villa exactly what they are missing in their current side.

“He is strong, inside the area he is devastating.

“He has quickness in his control, in moving the ball, in shooting, and he is composed in front of goal. For us he is an extra weapon. We are keeping him close and we hope he continues like this in these last two matches.”.

When Malen signed for Aston Villa, he had a reputation for being a goalscoring winger with great pace, but Emery seemed to never fully trust him, and ultimately his place in the team was never assured.

Now that he has gone over to Italy, he is showing what could have happened if he had been given that trust. He is scoring goals for fun in a league that is best known for its defensive qualities, and is making it look easy.

In a recent development, if Emery had ever given him that opportunity, then it may be that the sale of Watkins wouldn't have been such an glitch. They would have already had a reliable source of goals in the squad, and there would be less pressure on Jackson and youngster Brian Madjo to hit the ground running.

The manager allowed several key players to leave in the summer, but it now seems clear that his biggest mistake was letting Malen leave and not replacing him properly.

It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola mentioned ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”.

Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike remain long-term absentees for the hosts with Jeremie Frimpong also missing. Florian Wirtz could feature despite going off with an ankle knock during the win over Brighton.

In a recent development, like Liverpool, Chelsea also had an all-Premier League tie in the third round of this competition, beating Leeds 6-3 in a high-scoring affair at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea come into tonight’s game off the back of a 2-0 defeat against Tottenham in the league last weekend. Not only did they lose on Saturday but to make matters worse for them Cole Palmer was sent off. As a result of that red card, Palmer is suspended for tonight’s tie.

“We [Alonso and Palmer] spoke and for sure he knows the mistake he made,” Alonso remarked. “Things that you can avoid. I hope that this is not going to be repeated. He is aware of that, he is mature and it was a mistake. He is in a good space, he connects very well socially with his teammates. They like him, they want Cole smiling, they want Cole having fun, enjoying his game because when we see that, he will have a better team. I will just ask you because he has got this very cool persona, you probably know his personality is very interesting.”.

According to recent reports, former Liverpool midfielder and current Chelsea boss Alonso has lost his two games as a manager against Liverpool; a 4-0 defeat as Bayer Leverkusen boss and then a 1-0 loss when in charge of Real Madrid, with both taking place at Anfield. Alonso is not the only ex-Liverpool midfielder to return to Anfield tonight as their former captain Jordan Henderson is in the Chelsea squad for tonight. Joao Pedro has missed the trip to Anfield because of a thigh injury which could rule him out for a few weeks.

The Premier league fixture between these sides at Anfield ended in a 1-1 draw back in May. In that match, Arne Slot was in charge of Liverpool with Calum McFarlane in interim charge of Chelsea. Chelsea won the reverse fixture 2-1 at Stamford Bridge. Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

Serie A | Napoli 1-0 Torino: McTominay to the rescue

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Napoli scraped a 1-0 victory over Torino thanks to Scott McTominay, but Antonio Vergara sustained a new injury and the woodwork rescued them from Rolando Mandragora.
  • The Partenopei reshuffled amid the usual injury crisis, as Alex Meret was ruled out by a couple of months, joining Benoit Badiashile, Alisson Santos, Stanislav Lobotka, Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Alessandro Buongiorno on the absentee list.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Napoli scraped a 1-0 victory over Torino thanks to Scott McTominay, but Antonio Vergara sustained a new injury and the woodwork rescued them from Rolando Mandragora.

The Partenopei reshuffled amid the usual injury crisis, as Alex Meret was ruled out by a couple of months, joining Benoit Badiashile, Alisson Santos, Stanislav Lobotka, Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Alessandro Buongiorno on the absentee list.

Sources indicate that they moved to a 3-5-2 formation, with Vanja Milinkovic-Savic facing his former club, and Scotland internationals Scott McTominay, Billy Gilmour and Che Adams all starting. Kevin De Bruyne was rested ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League trip to Manchester City. Toro had one point from the last three rounds going into the break for international duty, but Giovanni Simeone was against his old teammates, with only Franco Israel missing.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

McTominay’s angled drive flashed wide of the far post, then Lucas Perri got down well to parry the Matteo Politano finish, with Ardian Ismajli preventing McTominay turning in the rebound.

Antonio Vergara was visibly distraught after picking up a muscular injury, limping off the field in tears after just 11 minutes to make way for De Bruyne.

McTominay’s deflected effort was fingertipped round the far post by Perri, then the Toro goalkeeper made a fine save on Rasmus Hojlund from a De Bruyne slide-rule pass.

Hojlund nodded the Leonardo Spinazzola cross over from seven yards, then moments later De Bruyne’s diving header from 10 yards was charged down by Saul Coco.

According to recent reports, torino were also forced into a change, as Rafik Belghali had a knee injury, replaced by Zakaria Aboukhlal. Nonetheless, they nearly took the lead on the stroke of half-time with a Rolando Mandragora screamer from distance that smacked against the crossbar.

The Granata pushed after the restart too, as Zakaria Aboukhlal saw his angled drive flash across the face of goal to skim the far post, then Simeone didn’t make the most of the situation when he caught Rafa Marin napping.

McTominay stung Perri’s gloves on a De Bruyne assist, while Mandragora’s free kick went around the wall to force a difficult Milinkovic-Savic save at the near post.

Perri parried the attempts from Noa Lang and Politano, then had more difficulty with the Hojlund strike from just inside the area.

It has been revealed that ardian Ismajli was forced off by a muscular issue, and Napoli took the lead moments later. Lang sprinted after Aboukhlal to stop the counter-attack, immediately turning it into an attacking situation by finding McTominay, who drilled into the far bottom corner from the edge of the box.

Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa threw himself in the path of a Cesare Casadei volley on a corner, and Duvan Zapata nodded the Mandragora corner wide.

With the last kick of the game, Lang went on the counter from a Torino corner, but Perri stuck out a boot to deny the angled drive.

Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla owner Elon Musk said on Friday that the company would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.
  • The South African entrepreneur said Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.
  • "Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk said on his X social media site.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla owner Elon Musk said on Friday that the company would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.

The South African entrepreneur said Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk said on his X social media site.

The announcement follows a bruising week for Musk amid the US midterm elections, where Republicans struggled despite his major donations, with his companies losing billions in value by market capitalization as investors sought to ditch stock.

Musk later responded to a complimentary user online who hailed the Cybertruck as the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made," and calling it an "end of an era" by saying: "True.".

For years he had poured much of his enthusiastic marketing zeal into promoting the Cybertruck, saying during the 2023 launch "finally, the future will look like the future.".

However the oversized body, straight lines and stainless steel and the post-apocalpytic vibe these created also met with widespread criticism and even mockery.

The electric powertrain was probably a barrier to sales in the US, by far the biggest pickup truck market, where Musk had hoped to take on some of the country's top-selling gas-guzzling vehicles like the Ford F150 or the Chevrolet Silverado and the Dodge Ram.

Meanwhile, the car's striking shape, weight and size made it impossible for Tesla to try to crack Europe, where electric vehicles are gaining a much larger market share.

Unlike in the US, EU safety regulations place considerable emphasis not just on people in cars in accidents, but also on the dangers posed to pedestrians who might be hit by a vehicle. That meant it was not possible for Tesla to register and sell the Cybertruck for road use in Europe.

Beyond this, the vehicle's size would likely have rendered it impractical and unpopular on many European roads, where space tends to be at more of a premium.

Depending how quick the wind-down proves to be, the Cybertruck's production run could prove shorter than its five-year R&D phase.

Given its longstanding problems meeting Musk's very public sales and production predictions, Tesla does not publish sales figures broken down by model.

But according to the automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the tech giant sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down from 38,965 in 2024.

At launch in 2023, Musk had predicted unit sales nearer a quarter of a million.

According to recent reports, for orientation, Ford sold more than 800,000 F-Series pickups in the US last year, a slight boost on 2024's numbers. These vehicles start at less than half the list price of a Cybertruck in the US.

Sources indicate that the IPO for SpaceX this year revealed that Musk's second-largest company was comfortably the biggest buyer of Cybertrucks in 2025. It bought vehicles worth $131 million and did not even enjoy a bulk-buy or friends-rate discount, paying list prices for the fleet.

The Cybercab is a vehicular element in Musk's bid to transform Tesla towards a tech giant focused more on AI and robotics than automobilies.

Rather than just featuring the self-drive or driving assistance programs that Musk has been championing for years, the Cybercab has no steering wheels, pedals or mirrors at all and is designed never to have a human in control.

Musk say the model will be the company's main autonomous model and will supply a global network of Robotaxis.

Starting in the past few months, around 300 such vehicles have been registered and have started operating, on approved roads in the Austin area near Tesla's Gigafactory Texas. They're being added to the existing fleet of autonomous Model Y Teslas being used for the purpose, serving in an area known as a geofence of around 680 square kilometers (264 square miles).

KILMARNOCK 2 ABERDEEN 4: Dazzling Dons get a Frick pick-up but it's more misery for McCann's men

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.
  • In Mario Frick, they may have got their man.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.

In Mario Frick, they may have got their man. Whether or not the former Luzern boss will be a success at Pittodrie is anyone’s guess. But on this evidence, it’s going to be a lot of fun watching him have a go.

At times, they were scintillating here on their way to a thrilling win which moved them five clear of their hosts and provided some much-needed breathing room ahead of a tricky upcoming schedule which involves trips to Ibrox and Tynecastle, as well as two home clashes against the Dundee clubs.

Yes, it wasn’t perfect. Far from it, in fact. Defensively, they were far too open. Kilmarnock just weren’t good enough to take full advantage.

But you suspect that will be forgiven to an extent as long as they can play with this level of panache and aggression going forward.

Findlay Marshall celebrates after scoring the Dons' fourth goal at Rugby Park.

It has been revealed that frick has arrived with the promise of bringing ‘heavy metal’ football to Pittodrie. It’s taken a little over 90 minutes to understand what he's talking about.

Industry observers note that ‘It was very chaotic,’ he admitted. ‘It's quite different to Switzerland, because there is technicality, but it’s not as physical as it was today.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It was difficult. We were lucky as well because Killie, especially in the second half, played very well, but I think at the end it's a deserved victory.

‘When the players were young, they didn’t think about mistakes, didn’t think about any negatives.

‘They played only to win for fun, and I told them to play as if they were young players and I think, especially first half, it was very good.

‘You don't know what's going on or what can happen in this first game, so I'm very happy we won.’.

Frick indicates his delight after tasting victory in his first match in charge of Aberdeen.

Kilmarnock spurned a golden opportunity to take a sixth-minute lead at the end of a rapid counter-attack, with Joe Hugill finding himself all alone in the Dons box.

The striker took a heavy first touch, allowing Marius Muller to swiftly narrow the angle and block the effort. It’s easy to see why Hugill has found the back of the net just twice this year.

And the hosts were made to pay for that miss within 90 seconds as Aberdeen went in front.

It has been revealed that for the umpteenth time this season, Killie failed to clear their lines under little pressure, with Stuart Armstrong teeing up Kevin Nisbet to sweep home a lovely finish from the edge of the area. The unsighted Nico Mantl in the Killie goal didn’t even move.

Mind you, he should have done significantly better four minutes later as Nisbet notched his second of the afternoon.

The keeper’s positioning as the Dons striker stepped up to send a low free-kick in off the post was as poor as it gets.

You got the feeling that the walls would have caved in had Aberdeen grabbed a third, but a brief drop-off in intensity from Frick’s side enabled Killie to drag themselves back into the contest.

A bit of pinball outside the Dons box saw the ball fall favourably for skipper Greg Kiltie 12 yards out, who adjusted his body brilliantly to drill beyond Muller on the half-volley.

Yet with a defence as dodgy as this, manager Neil McCann can never feel overly confident.

Ante Palaversa – terrific on his first appearance of the season – was given far too much time in the centre circle to get his head up and pick out Nesta Guinness-Walker on the left.

He glided past MJ Kamson-Kamara as if he wasn’t there before dinking a ball right on to the head of Brad Lyons, who rose completely unopposed to power home against his former employers.

Industry observers note that if Killie continue to defend like this, relegation is a certainty. Will the manager even get the chance to turn it around? Going off the abuse being hurled in his direction from the home punters, his jacket is evidently on a shoogly peg. Many fans have already made up their mind.

Nisbet's free-kick finds the net for his second as the Dons take control of the game.

Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s deflected effort from 20 yards shortly after the restart looked destined for the goal before Muller instinctively leapt to his right to claw it away on the line. It was a superb stop.

His next contribution defied belief.

Goodness knows what the keeper was thinking as he tried to pass out from the six-yard line, playing it straight to the feet of Tyreece John-Jules – only just on the park – who steadied himself before finishing.

You would have stuck your house on Nisbet putting this one to bed with five minutes remaining, however with just Mantl to beat, he pulled his left-footed effort wide.

Findlay Marshall showed him how it’s done with stoppage-time looming, running half the length of the field before drilling low into the corner to consign Killie to another sobering defeat.

McCann said: ‘I probably sound like a broken record, but we create really big, big chances, and we don't take them.

‘We're letting games pass us by. We're giving teams the opportunity to start ahead of us because of the goals we're conceding and then it's difficult to work back.’.

#94462. Breaking: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability

Breaking: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1005 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.
  • If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.
  • It has been revealed that france's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

It has been revealed that france's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

Germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

It has been revealed that as a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.

The spread acts as a kind of "fever gauge" for bond markets, explained Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

It has been revealed that "This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide toward a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he said.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fueled spending spree to end anytime soon.

It has been revealed that "French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE [the French national statistics agency — Editor's note], 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.

For more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.

Industry observers note that france last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how quickly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

According to recent reports, the main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and the recent unrest.

It has been revealed that the higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

These figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is currently estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Tresor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.

It has been revealed that the trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

"For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warned the economist.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

Industry observers note that RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire.".

"Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he has claimed.

For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales.".

Their common message, he noted, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts.".

Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.

"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," he pointed out.

"In the past, currency devaluations [of the French franc — Editor's note] made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier noted.

This article was originally written in German.

Industry News: Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot

💡 Key Takeaways
  • David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.
  • Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others.
  • Industry observers note that what a happy change of direction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

Industry observers note that what a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

Industry observers note that the lack of discipline in their ranks was exposed when Dan Burn scored a late consolation and ended up in a melee with James Tarkowski and Joelinton. But the issues Jaissle, who lamented that “we must improve”, has to correct are for another day: this contest belonged to Everton.

In a recent development, thierno Barry had provided the finish that secured a trip to Fleetwood in December and what an opportunity it is for Moyes to make Everton semi-finalists in this competition for the first time since 2016. Whether Grealish will have a part to play in it remains to be seen.

Thierno Barry with Everton's third! 🔵 https://t.co/dyb8fKud8N.

Industry observers note that the last thing Everton needed on a night of such importance was a distraction. Grealish will have a tough job mending relations, particularly with Moyes, but there was a paradox: though he had caused a major problem for 90 minutes he became an irrelevance.

Moyes is impatient to give Evertonians a big day out and his only focus was on crossing this hurdle – for all that Newcastle have had a turbulent start to the campaign, they are dangerous opponents and you wondered in the fraught opening 30 minutes if they might exacerbate the hosts’ woes.

As Jaissle hopped and squirmed on the sidelines, imploring Newcastle forward, chances came and went: Harvey Barnes had a header saved, Fabian Schar tested Jordan Pickford from 30 yards while Vitalii Mykolenko and James Tarkowski made huge goal-saving challenges.

In a recent development, “We should have scored more goals,” Jaissle, who was dressed as if auditioning for the role of The Milk Tray Man, growled. “It [losing] was shocking as the game was not that bad.”.

Moyes was infuriated by Everton’s initial inertia, so much so there was a point when the Scot prevented Merlin Röhl, his own full-back, from taking a throw-in until Tarkowski and Jake O’Brien had complied with his gesturing to get 10 yards further forward.

It might have looked old-fashioned but it worked. Suddenly Everton started asking questions, Hayden Hackney almost got on the end of a cross from Mykolenko, and it encouraged the supporters on the vertiginous South Stand to raise their voices and become more involved.

Sources indicate that what they needed was a goal to set things alight and in the 34th minute, it arrived. Tyrique George won possession by Newcastle’s corner flag, the ball dropped at Hackney’s feet and he instinctively ushered it on to James Garner, who whipped a right-footed drive beyond Lukáš Horníček.

James Garner puts Everton in front against Newcastle in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 https://t.co/TzponbWyGU.

The roar that greeted it was a mix of elation and wonder, relief and desperation. The locals have grown weary of seeing nights with potential end in disappointment but here was the foothold they craved and the opportunity they were ready to seize. Soon the lead would be doubled.

Hackney would score the goal, converting a super Barry cross, but let us acknowledge the fabulous refereeing of Farai Hallam, who waved play on when he might have whistled for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. And how Everton took advantage.

In a recent development, hayden Hackney doubles Everton's advantage! 🔵 https://t.co/VIY0Iln3nI.

Industry observers note that it must be said the officiating this week has, in the main, been outstanding. Watching a match without the persistent spectre of VAR has been liberating and you can see the referees have felt free to make decisions on instinct.

Industry observers note that the whole experience of knowing a contest cannot be re-refereed has been better for all. It will not catch on, sadly, because too many people have gone too far down the road with VAR, but we should embrace the purity of “old school football” while we can.

Evertonians – the Prime Minister included – certainly embraced the buffer of a second goal and the fact Hackney scored it also felt like a throwback: a player who was plucked out of the Championship in the summer and encouraged by Moyes to show he could make the next step up.

He did that and so, too, did Everton, their progress was assured in the 69th minute when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall dashed down the left and crossed for Barry to finish. Moyes puffed out his cheeks as it hit the net. He, more than most, deserved to enjoy this one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shania Twain is standing up for others in country music.

The legendary star in the genre used her acceptance speech for the Equal Play Award at Sunday’s CMT Awards to call for more equity and diversity in the country music industry.

In a recent development, “When I wrote the phrase ‘Man I feel like a woman’ I honestly had no idea at the time it would become an undercurrent of a decades-long career,” she said, referring to one of her biggest hits. “It’s amazing how one statement can empower so many.”.

The phrase, Twain mentioned, “has been adopted by an array of fantastic communities all around the world and become a genuine path of power…which brings me so much joy.”.

Sources indicate that “I believe in an all-inclusive country music. We’re family,” Twain said. “This is a genre of music with a rich history that raised and nurtured my own songwriting and performance and recording career from childhood. Presently, the industry standard does a real disservice to this.”.

Twain, who was presented the award by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, shouted out some of the diverse acts she is spotlighting on her “Queen of Me” tour this year, including Lily Rose, Lindsay Ell, Hailey Whitters, Mickey Guyton and others.

“I will continue to do my best as a trailblazer,” Twain noted. “Together, let’s ensure all our fellow artists get equal play regardless of gender, age or race.”.

She also performed acappella with the African American singing group, The BoykinZ, while presenting an award onstage. Twain connected with the group, who are sisters and rising country stars, after Kelly Clarkson surprised them recently by bringing Twain out to meet them during an episode of Clarkson’s daytime talk show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Timing is everything in football - and that goes for getting transfer moves right, too.

After seven years at Chelsea, Willian made the move across London to join Arsenal in 2020, which seemed like it should be a decent enough fit for all concerned.

But Willian has made no secret of the fact that he did not enjoy his time at the Emirates Stadium - and in hindsight, he believes he may simply have been the wrong player in the wrong place at the wrong time.

According to recent reports, willian told FourFourTwo: "These things happen in football. I had some personal frustrations and I couldn't perform on the pitch the way I had been performing at Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that "Arsenal were also a club that was changing a lot at that time. There were a lot of people leaving and a lot of new people coming in.

"It was a restructuring and I got caught up in the middle of it - and it's not easy.

I left a well-established club, winning almost every year, fighting for titles every year, and I joined a club that was trying to find a way to win titles again.

Industry observers note that "So I got caught up in that situation, and that's why things didn't work out. It wasn't easy, but I really wasn't happy.

"The contract I had was actually a very substantial one, but it got to the point that money wasn’t enough.

"The most important thing is to be happy, to play with joy. I wasn't able to do so there, so I ended up asking to leave the club, leaving that contract behind.".

After spending a year back in Brazil with Corinthians, Willian found a new home at Fulham in 2022 - and he credits Marco Silva with helping him to rediscover his spark.

He said: "When I left Brazil, my goal was to go to England, stay there, because I love the place and my agent lives there too.

"Therefore, I decided to be in London, have some meetings and see what the possibilities are. My agent noted, ‘Marco Silva wants to talk to you’. We had a meeting with him, and he invited me to join training and see how I felt.

"It wasn't a trial, it was more to see if I could readjust, especially after what had happened to me at Arsenal.

Industry observers note that "I really liked Marco’s style. I felt celebrated, and it's not flattery, but I felt that respect, that affection from everyone. I was very happy there at Fulham.".

Spain won 2-0 in Prague despite missing Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Oyarzabal, with Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena converting a penalty and Marc Pubill adding a late second. The win keeps the world champions perfect in Nations League Group A3 and leaves them needing only a draw against England on Sunday.

It has been revealed that spain beat ten-man Czechia 2-0 at the Letná Stadium in Prague on Thursday. They did it without three of their leading names. Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Oyarzabal were all missing. Atlético Madrid’s Álex Baena struck from the spot, and Marc Pubill added a late second. The world champions remain perfect in Group A3 before Sunday’s decider against England.

In a recent development, conditions were raw. The game was played in 4°C, with light drizzle and humidity above 90%, the Spanish federation said. Czechia are coached by the Spaniard Santi Denia.

Chances were scarce before the break. Dean Huijsen’s header was Spain’s only open-play effort on target in the first half, and it was easily saved. The breakthrough came from the penalty spot. Lukáš Ambros was penalised for handball in the area. Baena’s powerful penalty beat goalkeeper Matěj Kovář.

According to recent reports, spain thought they had doubled the lead after half-time. VAR ruled out an effort by Yéremy Pino. The game was physical. Referee Nikola Dabanovic booked Pedro Porro in the 12th minute and Mikel Merino in the 69th. He then dismissed Krejčí, leaving the hosts a man down for the closing stages.

It has been revealed that spain made the extra man count deep into added time. Pubill won the ball back in Czechia’s half and rolled it into the bottom corner. That settled the contest. For Atlético followers, Baena’s goal was the night’s highlight. Fermín López, by contrast, is still waiting for his first Spain goal.

According to recent reports, the victory was Spain’s 12th in a row and their fifth straight win in the Nations League. ESPN stated it stretched their record unbeaten run in all competitions. Spain’s last defeat came against Colombia in March 2024. Czechia, meanwhile, have lost every Nations League game this season.

It has been revealed that england kept pace on the same night. They beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley and sit three points behind Spain. That sets up a straight shoot-out for first place. A draw against England at the Metropolitano on Sunday will be enough for Spain to finish first in the group.
